purpose: Known feasible controller candidates for the four fixed tasks. These are engineering references, not Astra or Sol results, and are not model inputs.
verification: All four candidates succeeded in local physics checks. The warehouse candidate was reverified after upstream commit 99534df changed parcel/deck physics. The new car controller task was verified at its declared fixed 22 m/s approach speed. Dog/drone results remain from their earlier unchanged-world checks.
evaluation_rule: Judge each model by fresh execution against the unchanged task criteria, not by equality with these parameter values. Other valid solutions may exist.

quadruped_gait_failure.explanation: Reduce the rear-leg gait-clock response to the speed increase so the original walking-speed schedule can finish without destabilizing the body.
quadruped_gait_failure.fixed_task: Original 18-second walk and speed increase; retain forward progress, requested-speed tracking, balance and contact criteria.
quadruped_gait_failure.verification_source: Earlier bounded engineering feasibility check reported by the dog adapter author; boundary tests are in tests/test_control_dog.py. The full corrected trace was not saved.

drone_delivery_imbalance.explanation: Maintain attitude trim while traveling, strengthen route attitude feedback, allow adequate compensation, and clear accumulated trim when support or payload release changes the load.
drone_delivery_imbalance.fixed_task: Take off at A with the parcel, release it supported and settled at B, fly back unloaded and land at A within 30 seconds, without in-flight body contact or a crash.
drone_delivery_imbalance.baseline_provenance: The tested baseline is a public-feedback port of the nominal controller in the same original physical world. It retains the outbound crash but is not a bit-identical stock-controller replay.
drone_delivery_imbalance.verification_source: Previously executed tests/test_control_drone.py::test_controller_adjustment_completes_delivery_release_return_and_landing, plus the adapter author's recorded engineering summary.

warehouse_curve_demo.explanation: Reduce the commanded trolley speed so the cargo remains aboard through the 90-degree turn while still completing the original route within its deadline.
warehouse_curve_demo.fixed_task: Complete the original approximately 7.285-metre route in the full 17-second trial, satisfying endpoint, heading and route-following criteria with cargo on deck and no cargo-floor contact.
warehouse_curve_demo.verification_source: Two new full physical trials on the merged 99534df scene, saved with complete baseline/reference telemetry and source hashes under runs/reference-warehouse-99534df. No model API calls were used for this feasibility check.

car_auto_brake_failure.explanation: Apply the same full brake pedal earlier so the physically conditioned car has enough distance to stop in the unchanged green target.
car_auto_brake_failure.fixed_task: Approach at 22 m/s after the original four physical conditioning cycles, and stop with the front bumper in x=86..98 m, at least 2 m before the wall at x=100 m. Remain below 0.1 m/s for one second and finish within 12 seconds without contact. Both controller candidates use this same fixed task.
car_auto_brake_failure.baseline_provenance: This controller task is calibrated at a fixed 22 m/s approach speed; the legacy 25 m/s failure replay remains unchanged. The physical car, four conditioning cycles, brake mechanics, wall and target are preserved.
car_auto_brake_failure.verification_source: Focused baseline and reference physical trials through investigation.task_recording.record_task without frames or model API calls. Complete corrected public telemetry and source hashes are saved under runs/reference-car-green-zone-20260910; the original baseline RGB preview is recorded separately under runs/preview-control-car.
